sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代在夜店打碟的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件最珍爱的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的、犹如50年前精美艺术品的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自奥彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, from shithole to shutdown, the story of the past week from the perspective of the only Democrat in the room when the president's now infamous remarks started it all.
sentences.zh: 今天，从屎坑国到政府关门，回顾过去一周的故事，视角来自总统那番如今已臭名昭著的言论引发一切时在场的唯一民主党人。

sentences.en: And if there is a shutdown, whose fault will it be?
sentences.zh: 如果政府真的关门了，那会是谁的错？

sentences.en: It's Friday, January 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月19日，星期五。

sentences.en: So is the bipartisan effort to pass immigration reform dead in the water?
sentences.zh: 那么，通过移民改革的两党努力是不是已经彻底泡汤了？

sentences.en: President Trump tweeting late this afternoon, Senator Dickey Durbin.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统今天下午晚些时候发推特称，参议员迪基·德宾。

sentences.en: Senator Dickey Durbin.
sentences.zh: 参议员迪基·德宾。

sentences.en: Senator Dickey Durbin.
sentences.zh: 参议员迪基·德宾。

sentences.en: Senator Dickey Durbin totally misrepresented what was said at the DACA meeting.
sentences.zh: 参议员迪基·德宾完全歪曲了DACA会议上所说的话。

sentences.en: Deals can't get made when there is no truSt.
sentences.zh: 没有信任就无法达成交易。

sentences.en: Durbin blew DACA and is hurting our military.
sentences.zh: 德宾搞砸了DACA，并且正在伤害我们的军队。

sentences.en: When was the last time anyone called you Dickey?
sentences.zh: 上一次有人叫你迪基是什么时候？

sentences.en: When I was about four years old.
sentences.zh: 大概在我四岁的时候吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, that one I just hadn't heard before.
sentences.zh: 是的，那个称呼我之前确实没听过。

sentences.en: I remember, and my mother hated it and told all of our relatives, stop calling him Dickey.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我母亲非常讨厌这个称呼，并告诉我们所有的亲戚，别再叫他迪基了。

sentences.en: I wish my mom were here, she could call the president.
sentences.zh: 我希望我妈妈现在还在这里，她可以给总统打电话。

sentences.en: She would be on the phone.
sentences.zh: 她肯定会打通电话的。

sentences.en: On Thursday morning, my colleague Carl Hulse spoke to Senator Dick Durbin about how much has changed since his meetings with the president last week,
sentences.zh: 周四上午，我的同事卡尔·赫尔斯采访了参议员迪克·德宾，谈到了自从他上周与总统会面以来情况发生了多大变化，

sentences.en: when the two were discussing the terms of a bipartisan immigration deal.
sentences.zh: 当时两人正在讨论两党移民协议的条款。

sentences.en: The first meeting was on Tuesday in the cabinet room, 26 of us, and the president asked me to sit next to him.
sentences.zh: 第一次会议是周二在内阁会议室举行的，我们有26个人，总统邀请我坐在他旁边。

sentences.en: That was the fourth time I ever had a conversation with the president.
sentences.zh: 那是我第四次和总统对话。

sentences.en: During the course of the meeting, he kept referring to, Dick and I agree, and I'm thinking, goodness, I mean, I've really come into high cotton here.
sentences.zh: 在会议期间，他一直提到，迪克和我意见一致，我当时想，天哪，我这可真算是飞黄腾达了。

sentences.en: He said several times, send me a bill and I'll sign it.
sentences.zh: 他说了好几次，给我送个法案来，我就签。

sentences.en: We've got to do this.
sentences.zh: 我们必须这么做。

sentences.en: There's no reason to delay it.
sentences.zh: 没有任何理由拖延。

sentences.en: And so I came back.
sentences.zh: 所以我回来了。

sentences.en: This group we've been negotiating with, bipartisan Senate group, we've been working together for months.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在谈判的这个群体，两党参议员小组，我们已经合作好几个月了。

sentences.en: I said, we've got to close this deal.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们必须敲定这笔交易。

sentences.en: The president's ready to go.
sentences.zh: 总统已经准备好了。

sentences.en: And we did in a matter of 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 我们在24小时内就做到了。

sentences.en: And I called the president back, because he'd asked me to, on Thursday morning at 10 o'clock and said, Mr. President, we have a bipartisan agreement in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我给总统回了电话，因为他在周四上午10点要求我这么做，我说，总统先生，我们在参议院达成了一项两党协议。

sentences.en: It hits all four points you raised.
sentences.zh: 它完全符合您提出的所有四点要求。

sentences.en: Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina is coming over to explain it to you.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州的参议员林赛·格雷厄姆正赶过来向您解释。

sentences.en: Great, he said.
sentences.zh: 太好了，他说。

sentences.en: I don't want to slow walk this.
sentences.zh: 我不想拖延。

sentences.en: Let's get this done.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这事办了。

sentences.en: So Lindsey and I, two hours later, two hours after this phone call, were scheduled to be in the Oval Office with the president.
sentences.zh: 所以林赛和我，在两小时后，在这通电话两小时后，按计划将与总统一起在椭圆形办公室会面。

sentences.en: The big shock was when we looked and saw we weren't the only ones invited.
sentences.zh: 最大的震惊是，当我们看过去时，发现被邀请的不止我们俩。

sentences.en: In a matter of two hours, someone had called five other members of Congress, two senators and three House members,
sentences.zh: 在短短两个小时内，有人打电话给其他五名国会议员，包括两名参议员和三名众议员，

sentences.en: most of whom have a pretty virulent opposition to any immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数对任何移民改革都抱有相当激烈的反对态度。

sentences.en: So the deck was stacked against us as the president walked in the room.
sentences.zh: 所以当总统走进房间时，局势对我们极其不利。

sentences.en: And so how then did the discussion go?
sentences.zh: 那么之后的讨论进展如何呢？

sentences.en: Did it start out immediately contentious?
sentences.zh: 一开始就很具有对抗性吗？

sentences.en: I mean, did he sit down and just say, well, I can't take this deal?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他坐下来就直接说，嗯，我不能接受这笔交易吗？

sentences.en: It started off with Lindsey Graham sitting right next to the president, describing what we'd agreed to.
sentences.zh: 一开始是林赛·格雷厄姆坐在总统旁边，描述我们达成的协议。

sentences.en: And he barely had a sentence or two out of his mouth.
sentences.zh: 他话还没说完一两句。

sentences.en: Then the president started commenting.
sentences.zh: 然后总统就开始发表评论了。

sentences.en: Who is affected by that?
sentences.zh: 谁会受到影响？

sentences.en: What is this going to do?
sentences.zh: 这会带来什么影响？

sentences.en: It was a very tough conversation starting immediately.
sentences.zh: 这是一场一开始就非常艰难的对话。

sentences.en: The president, who was so open two hours before, was not open when we talked to him in the Oval Office.
sentences.zh: 两个小时前还那么开明的总统，当我们在椭圆形办公室与他交谈时却不再开明了。

sentences.en: Now, you didn't push back on the president in the meeting, but Lindsey Graham did from your account.
sentences.zh: 现在，你在会议上没有回击总统，但据你的说法，林赛·格雷厄姆回击了。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实回击了。

sentences.en: And I'm glad he did, because it was a moment I thought to myself, Durbin, what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 我很高兴他这么做了，因为当时我在心里想，德宾，你打算怎么办？

sentences.en: You just can't sit here silently.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是坐在这里保持沉默。

sentences.en: Right, so this is in your brain.
sentences.zh: 对，所以这是在你脑海里盘旋。

sentences.en: Even if it's the president.
sentences.zh: 即使对方是总统。

sentences.en: And Lindsey stepped in.
sentences.zh: 然后林赛介入了。

sentences.en: And bless him, he gave the most articulate, extemporaneous defense of American immigration that I could ever ask for.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑他，他发表了我所能要求的对美国移民最清晰、最即兴的辩护。

sentences.en: And he was very explicit.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常明确。

sentences.en: He used the vulgar term which the president used, repeated it to him in describing his own family circumstance.
sentences.zh: 他使用了总统用过的那个粗俗词汇，在描述他自己的家庭情况时向总统重复了这句话。

sentences.en: I've complimented him publicly and privately over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我公开和私下都一次又一次地称赞过他。

sentences.en: It was a great statement.
sentences.zh: 那是一份很棒的陈述。

sentences.en: I spoke up on a number of issues.
sentences.zh: 我在许多问题上都发言了。

sentences.en: I said, if you separate the Haitians from the El Salvadorans and the Hondurans who are here under temporary protected status, it's pretty obvious what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我说，如果你把海地人与根据临时保护身份来到这里的萨尔瓦多人和洪都拉斯人分开，你在做什么就显而易见了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an obvious racial decision.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个显而易见的种族决定。

sentences.en: You were the only Democrat in the room, I think, as far as I know.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，你是房间里唯一的民主党人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Do you think that there's any possibility that he kind of just forgot that or just didn't hold back?
sentences.zh: 你认为有没有可能他只是把这事给忘了，或者只是没有克制自己？

sentences.en: I don't know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道答案是什么。

sentences.en: But as I looked around the room, yes, I was the only one there from the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 但当我环顾房间时，是的，我是那里唯一来自民主党的人。

sentences.en: So, you know, we've both been in politics a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们俩从事政治都很长时间了。

sentences.en: People talk differently behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 人们在闭门会谈时的说法是不一样的。

sentences.en: And you've been in these discussions.
sentences.zh: 你也参加过这些讨论。

sentences.en: But this was beyond what you would normally.
sentences.zh: 但这超出了你通常会遇到的情况。

sentences.en: It was beyond.
sentences.zh: 这确实超出了常规。

sentences.en: And after Lindsay and I left the room and got in the car together to come back to Capitol Hill, it was silence in the car.
sentences.zh: 林赛和我离开房间一起上车返回国会山后，车里一片寂静。

sentences.en: We just witnessed something that neither one of us ever expected.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚目睹了我们俩都从未预料到的事情。

sentences.en: I came back here and the people, the senators I sat down and talked to immediately, there were four or five of them,
sentences.zh: 我回到这里，我坐下来立即交谈的人，有四五个参议员，

sentences.en: to describe exactly what happened as we tried to decide what to do next.
sentences.zh: 向他们准确描述了当我们试图决定下一步该怎么做时发生了什么。

sentences.en: They said, you look shaken.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你看起来很震惊。

sentences.en: I said I was.
sentences.zh: 我说我的确很震惊。

sentences.en: So this is a tricky question because I don't exactly know how this all came down.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个棘手的问题，因为我不太清楚这一切是如何泄露出去的。

sentences.en: And my understanding is that you did not leak this to the president.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，你并没有向外界透露这件事。

sentences.en: I did not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: And I instructed my staff not to.
sentences.zh: 我还指示我的工作人员不要透露。

sentences.en: So would you have preferred in some ways this hadn't come out because of the chaos it's caused in the DACA negotiations?
sentences.zh: 那么从某些方面来说，你是否希望这件事没有曝光，因为它给DACA谈判带来了混乱？

sentences.en: I think now that the American people have a clearer understanding of the president's motivation on immigration, it makes it easier to confront some of the things he's suggesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在美国人民对总统在移民问题上的动机有了更清晰的理解，这使得反驳他提出的某些观点变得更容易了。

sentences.en: If you remember from the campaign, this was all about security and terrorism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得竞选期间的情况，这完全是关于安全和恐怖主义的。

sentences.en: You know, these people are getting in here and they're dangerous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些人进来了，他们很危险。

sentences.en: Stop these Muslims and so forth.
sentences.zh: 阻止这些穆斯林等等。

sentences.en: Then it kind of moved to, no, we're really protecting American jobs.
sentences.zh: 然后它有点转向，不，我们实际上是在保护美国人的工作岗位。

sentences.en: Well, that Thursday meeting in the White House brought up another part of this debate, which had not surfaced before.
sentences.zh: 好吧，白宫周四的那次会议提出了这场辩论的另一个部分，这是之前没有浮出水面的。

sentences.en: And I think it is a major part of the president's calculus.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是总统盘算中的一个重要部分。

sentences.en: And so in the airing of this ultimately, you know, clears the air a little bit.
sentences.zh: 因此，这件事最终曝光，你知道，稍微澄清了一下空气。

sentences.en: And there's more of an honest discussion.
sentences.zh: 会有更多坦诚的讨论。

sentences.en: I think there's more of an honest discussion.
sentences.zh: 我认为会有更多坦诚的讨论。

sentences.en: I also think that when we look at the president's immigration policy, most of which I consider to be excessive and unfair,
sentences.zh: 我也认为，当我们审视总统的移民政策时，其中大部分我认为都是过分且不公平的，

sentences.en: that we'll put it in the context that this may not be about security or American jobs at all.
sentences.zh: 我们会将其置于这样的背景下：这可能根本不是关于安全或美国的工作岗位。

sentences.en: It's something else.
sentences.zh: 而是别的东西。

sentences.en: So do you think there might have to be a shutdown for a while to force the issue?
sentences.zh: 那你认为是否必须让政府关闭一段时间来迫使这个问题解决呢？

sentences.en: I think we can avoid it.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以避免这种情况。

sentences.en: I think what's going to happen here is you're going to have a bit of a pushback, if not a rebellion,
sentences.zh: 我认为接下来会发生的是，你将会看到来自两党成员的某种反弹，甚至是叛变，

sentences.en: from members of both political parties about the fact that we're on our fourth continuing resolution.
sentences.zh: 因为我们正处于第四个持续决议案阶段。

sentences.en: For your listeners, a continuing resolution is an excuse.
sentences.zh: 对于你的听众来说，持续决议案只是一个借口。

sentences.en: We can't agree on a budget.
sentences.zh: 我们无法就预算达成一致。

sentences.en: So we're just going to push the can down the road, as they say, for another few days.
sentences.zh: 所以正如他们所说，我们只能把问题往后拖延几天。

sentences.en: That's awful.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell is handing us this CR and saying to the Democrats, take it or leave it.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔把这个持续决议案交给我们，并对民主党人说，接受还是离开。

sentences.en: That is no way to run a government of the greatest country in the world.
sentences.zh: 这不是治理世界上最伟大国家政府的方式。

sentences.en: If there's a short-term CR without a DACA deal, do you vote for it?
sentences.zh: 如果在没有达成DACA协议的情况下出现短期持续决议案，你会投赞成票吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: So you're off.
sentences.zh: 所以你投反对票。

sentences.en: I'm off.
sentences.zh: 我投反对票。

sentences.en: Well, this is going to be an extremely interesting 48 hours or so here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，接下来的48小时左右这里将变得极其有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you, Senator.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，参议员。

sentences.en: Thanks for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报 DealBook 报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的舞台上现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些最具影响力的人物，包括J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日在NYTimes.com上免费直播精选采访，供任何人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: Jonathan, what are the conditions under which government shutdowns happen?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，政府关门是在什么条件和情况下发生的？

sentences.en: Let's look at the last time the government shut down.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看政府上一次关门是什么时候。

sentences.en: That was in 2013.
sentences.zh: 那是在2013年。

sentences.en: Jonathan Weissman covered that shutdown for The Times.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·韦斯曼为《时报》报道了那次政府关门。

sentences.en: Remember,
sentences.zh: 记住，

sentences.en: This legislation will not fix everything that ails our health care system, but it moves us decisively in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 这项立法无法解决我们医疗体系中存在的所有问题，但它使我们朝着正确的方向坚决迈进。

sentences.en: You have Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 你有贝拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: This is what change looks like.
sentences.zh: 这就是变革的样子。

sentences.en: The president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 美利坚合众国总统。

sentences.en: Well, I think that we need to repeal this bill and replace it with common sense reforms that'll bring down the cost of health insurance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们需要废除这项法案，并用常识性改革取而代之，以降低医疗保险的成本。

sentences.en: You have Republicans in control of the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 当时共和党人控制了众议院。

sentences.en: Democrats still had control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 民主党人仍然控制着参议院。

sentences.en: The leader of Senate Democrats, Harry Reid, has already made it clear there will be no defections on his side.
sentences.zh: 参议院民主党领袖哈里·里德已经明确表示，他这一方不会有人叛变。

sentences.en: Any bill that defunds Obamacare is dead.
sentences.zh: 任何取消奥巴马医改资金的法案都是死路一条。

sentences.en: Dead.
sentences.zh: 死路一条。

sentences.en: It's a waste of time, as I said before.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，这是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: And if I recall, in this mix, at this moment, are Tea Party Republicans who have just been elected, and they are particularly rancorous.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，在这个时候，刚刚当选的茶党共和党人也身处其中，他们尤其好斗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The Tea Party Republicans were swept into power in control of the House in 2011.
sentences.zh: 茶党共和党人在2011年席卷政坛，控制了众议院。

sentences.en: What's happened here?
sentences.zh: 这里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because all across the country, we have Republicans and Tea Party candidates making huge gains over Democrats.
sentences.zh: 因为放眼全国，我们看到共和党人和茶党候选人大幅战胜了民主党人。

sentences.en: The new Tea Party rising star, Ted Cruz from Texas.
sentences.zh: 茶党的新星，来自德克萨斯州的泰德·克鲁兹。

sentences.en: A Tea Party uprising of sorts nationwide.
sentences.zh: 全国各地爆发了某种形式的茶党起义。

sentences.en: Throw the bums out.
sentences.zh: 把这些混蛋赶出去。

sentences.en: And they're an angry bunch.
sentences.zh: 而且他们气势汹汹。

sentences.en: They want to show that they still have control of the House.
sentences.zh: 他们想要证明自己仍然掌控着众议院。

sentences.en: They can still push Barack Obama around.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然可以对巴拉克·奥巴马施压。

sentences.en: Time is running out to pass a spending bill and avoid a partial government shutdown on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 通过支出法案、避免周二部分政府关门的时间所剩无几。

sentences.en: But today...
sentences.zh: 但今天……

sentences.en: That's when Ted Cruz, the senator from Texas, decided no government spending can be approved by Congress unless it strips all money from the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，来自德克萨斯州的参议员泰德·克鲁兹决定，国会不得批准任何政府支出，除非剥离《平价医疗法案》的所有资金。

sentences.en: I intend to speak in support of defunding Obamacare until I am no longer able to stand.
sentences.zh: 我打算一直发表支持取消对“奥巴马医改”拨款的演讲，直到我站不起来为止。

sentences.en: Cruz went over to the House, and he actually went behind the backs of the Republican leadership.
sentences.zh: 克鲁兹去了众议院，甚至背着共和党领导层行事。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He met with House Republicans, some of those Tea Party guys, and he rallied them.
sentences.zh: 他会见了众议院共和党人，其中一些是茶党成员，并把他们聚集起来。

sentences.en: And he said, let's just not support any kind of spending bill that funds Obamacare, that doesn't kill Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 他说，让我们不要支持任何资助“奥巴马医改”、不能扼杀“奥巴马医改”的支出法案。

sentences.en: The evidence overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 证据确凿。

sentences.en: This law is a train wreck.
sentences.zh: 这项法律是一场灾难。

sentences.en: He inserts language into the House budget bill, the bill to keep the government funded, hoping
sentences.zh: 他在众议院的预算案中塞入了条款，即保持政府资金运转的法案，希望

sentences.en: that it would pass the House and somehow, I don't even know how, get through the Senate.
sentences.zh: 它能通过众议院，并且以某种方式——我甚至不知道是什么方式——在参议院获得通过。

sentences.en: The mainstream wing of the GOP is firing back, led by the Senate's top Republican,
sentences.zh: 共和党建制派正在进行反击，领头的是参议院共和党领袖

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell, who opened fire on the Ted Cruz wing of the party in the Wall Street Journal.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔，他在《华尔街日报》上向党内的泰德·克鲁兹派系猛烈开火。

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell, who said of Cruz's shutdown strategy, a tactical error.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔谈到克鲁兹的关门战略时称其为战术失误。

sentences.en: It was not a smart play.
sentences.zh: 这不是明智的举动。

sentences.en: It had no chance of success.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何成功的机会。

sentences.en: So Cruz is drawing a hard line among some Republicans, a line that seems impossible that the other side can accommodate.
sentences.zh: 因此，克鲁兹在部分共和党人中划出了一条强硬的红线，一条让对方看起来根本无法妥协的红线。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It was going to fail from the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 它从一开始就会失败。

sentences.en: Not only was there no way that President Obama was going to sign into law some kind of spending bill that got rid of Obamacare, but it was never going to pass the Senate.
sentences.zh: 不仅奥巴马总统绝不可能签署任何废除“奥巴马医改”的支出法案，而且它也绝无可能在参议院通过。

sentences.en: Because remember, the Senate needs 60 votes and the Democrats were never going to go along.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，参议院需要60票，而民主党人绝不会买账。

sentences.en: We're not going to be extorted.
sentences.zh: 我们不会接受敲诈。

sentences.en: The country is not going to be extorted.
sentences.zh: 这个国家不会被敲诈。

sentences.en: We're not going to negotiate with a gun to our heads.
sentences.zh: 我们不会在被人用枪指着头的情况下进行谈判。

sentences.en: We're not going to allow the Republicans to say, give us what we want or the economy is going to close.
sentences.zh: 我们不会允许共和党人说，给我们想要的，否则经济就会关门。

sentences.en: Think about that.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: So they just put it in their back pocket and they pass their own spending bill.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是把法案揣进自己口袋，通过了他们自己的支出法案。

sentences.en: The government's going to shut down in three days, 10 hours, five minutes and nine seconds.
sentences.zh: 政府将在三天十小时五分钟零九秒后关门。

sentences.en: The Senate has acted.
sentences.zh: 参议院已经采取了行动。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the House led by Cruz, who oddly enough is in the Senate, passes a bill that says we are going to try to kill the Affordable Care Act and link it to the budget.
sentences.zh: 因此，由克鲁兹（说来也巧，他本人在参议院）领导的众议院通过了一项法案，称我们将设法废除《平价医疗法案》，并将其与预算挂钩。

sentences.en: The Senate says that's never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 参议院表示这绝无可能发生。

sentences.en: So it passes its own more traditional bill that just keeps the government funded.
sentences.zh: 因此它通过了自身更为传统的法案，仅仅用于保持政府资金运转。

sentences.en: But of course, as we know from you, those two things have to be reconciled and they can't be reconciled.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如我们从你这里了解到的，这两者必须进行调和，而它们根本无法调和。

sentences.en: So then what happens?
sentences.zh: 那接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: It is now exactly midnight here on the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 现在东海岸时间正好是午夜。

sentences.en: And for the first time in 17 years, the American federal government is as of right now in the process of shutting down.
sentences.zh: 17年来第一次，美国联邦政府从现在这一刻起正处于关门的过程中。

sentences.en: The actual government shut down.
sentences.zh: 政府真的关门了。

sentences.en: While you were sleeping, Congress missed the midnight deadline to pass a crucial spending bill.
sentences.zh: 当你在睡觉时，国会错过了通过关键支出法案的午夜期限。

sentences.en: Lawmakers went back and forth and back and forth.
sentences.zh: 议员们反复拉锯。

sentences.en: And in the end, got nowhere.
sentences.zh: 结果却一无所获。

sentences.en: The government shuts down for 17 days.
sentences.zh: 政府关门了17天。

sentences.en: More than 5 million disabled veterans won't get their checks.
sentences.zh: 超过500万残疾退伍军人领不到支票。

sentences.en: The National Institutes of Health began turning away dozens of children, many suffering from cancer, from drug trials.
sentences.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院开始拒绝数十名儿童（其中许多患有癌症）参与药物试验。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of federal workers haven't been paid since...
sentences.zh: 成千上万的联邦雇员自……以来一直没有领到工资

sentences.en: I'm a line cook at the Smithsonian National Museum for the American Indian.
sentences.zh: 我是史密森尼美洲印第安人国家博物馆的一名熟食厨师。

sentences.en: Since the shutdown, I went from low wage to no wage.
sentences.zh: 自从政府关门后，我的收入从低薪变成了零薪水。

sentences.en: I'm a hardworking mother and I just want to let Washington know that it's not fair because we have, I have worked so hard to pay my taxes every year.
sentences.zh: 我是一位辛苦工作的母亲，我只想让华盛顿知道这很不公平，因为我们，我每年都非常努力地工作来纳税。

sentences.en: I mean, the government shut down and I wasn't ready for it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，政府关门了，而我毫无准备。

sentences.en: I mean, so now I'm out of work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在我失业了。

sentences.en: Real people are hurt by government shutdowns.
sentences.zh: 普通人正受到政府关门的伤害。

sentences.en: This Republican shutdown did not have to happen.
sentences.zh: 这场由共和党造成的政府关门本不必发生。

sentences.en: But I want every American to understand why it did happen.
sentences.zh: 但我希望每个美国人都明白它为什么会发生。

sentences.en: You know, when the government shuts down, it really signals to Americans that their hatred of
sentences.zh: 你知道，当政府关门时，它确实向美国人传递了一个信号：他们对

sentences.en: Washington is founded, that Washington doesn't function right.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的厌恶是有根据的，华盛顿运转不正常。

sentences.en: This really shows that Washington is just not working.
sentences.zh: 这充分表明华盛顿根本没有在运转。

sentences.en: Let me be more specific.
sentences.zh: 让我说得更具体一点。

sentences.en: One faction of one party in one House of Congress, in one branch of government,
sentences.zh: 国会一个院、一个政府部门里一个政党的一个派别，

sentences.en: shut down major parts of the government, all because they didn't like one law.
sentences.zh: 关闭了政府的主要部门，仅仅因为他们不喜欢一项法律。

sentences.en: The Democrats really played this.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在这场博弈中表现得很出色。

sentences.en: And of course, they have Obama in the White House.
sentences.zh: 当然，白宫里有奥巴马。

sentences.en: Obama has just been reelected.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马刚刚赢得连任。

sentences.en: He's pretty popular.
sentences.zh: 他相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: He's a lot more popular than House Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他比众议院共和党人受欢迎得多。

sentences.en: And so he's able to use the bully pulpit to frame this as irresponsibility on the part of the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 因此，他能够利用总统的崇高地位和话语权，将此定性为共和党人的不负责任。

sentences.en: Well, listen, we've been locked in a fight over here trying to bring government down to size, trying to do our best to stop Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们一直在这里陷入一场斗争，试图将政府规模缩减，尽最大努力阻止“奥巴马医改”。

sentences.en: And ultimately...
sentences.zh: 归根结底……

sentences.en: And so if they're going to hold on to their position that we're always going to raise taxes, then we're not going to come to the ground.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们坚持我们必须不断加税的立场，那么我们是不会做出妥协的。

sentences.en: John Boehner...
sentences.zh: 约翰·博纳……

sentences.en: Speaker of the House, right?
sentences.zh: 众议院议长，对吧？

sentences.en: ...goes to the Republicans and says, you have to just open the government.
sentences.zh: ……找到共和党人说，你们必须让政府重新开门。

sentences.en: We fought a good fight.
sentences.zh: 我们打了一场漂亮的仗。

sentences.en: We did everything we could to get them to the table and to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 我们尽了一切努力让他们回到谈判桌前进行谈判。

sentences.en: They just kept saying no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不停地说不、不、不、不。

sentences.en: And so we fought the good fight.
sentences.zh: 所以我们打了一场漂亮的仗。

sentences.en: There's just no reason for our members to vote no today.
sentences.zh: 我们的议员今天没有任何理由投反对票。

sentences.en: When will the government reopen?
sentences.zh: 政府什么时候重新开门？

sentences.en: I would expect this will happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我预计这将在明天发生。

sentences.en: And ultimately...
sentences.zh: 归根结底……

sentences.en: After weeks spent facing off across a partisan divide that often seemed too wide to cross...
sentences.zh: 经过数周在党派分歧之中的对峙，这种分歧往往看起来无法跨越……

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们做到了。

sentences.en: ...critical adversaries set aside their differences to reach this important agreement.
sentences.zh: ……关键对手搁置分歧，达成了这项重要协议。

sentences.en: They get nothing out of this entire fiasco.
sentences.zh: 他们在这场闹剧中一无所获。

sentences.en: They have not won a single concession.
sentences.zh: 他们没有赢得哪怕一次妥协。

sentences.en: And the government simply reopens.
sentences.zh: 政府就这样重新开门了。

sentences.en: The federal government shutdown is finally, finally over.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府关门终于、终于结束了。

sentences.en: After 16 days, 800,000 federal workers sent home, museums, zoos, and national parks closed, and an estimated $24 billion hit to the American economy.
sentences.zh: 在16天之后，80万联邦员工回家待命，博物馆、动物园和国家公园关闭，美国经济遭受了约240亿美元的打击。

sentences.en: And how does that ultimately affect this faction of Republicans, these Tea Party Republicans that started this all in 2013?
sentences.zh: 这最终如何影响这派共和党人，即在2013年挑起这一切的茶党共和党人？

sentences.en: I think you have to look at the political ramifications to understand where we are right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须着眼于政治后果，才能理解我们现在的处境。

sentences.en: Because at the time, the Republicans took a huge hit in the polling.
sentences.zh: 因为当时，共和党人在民调中遭受了巨大打击。

sentences.en: The American public are not happy, and they're especially angry at Republicans.
sentences.zh: 美国公众很不高兴，他们对共和党人格外愤怒。

sentences.en: And it looked like Democrats were going to have a real resurgence.
sentences.zh: 看起来民主党人将迎来真正的复苏。

sentences.en: The polling showed that Republicans were being blamed, and that their approval ratings were in the absolute toilet.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，共和党人正在受到指责，他们的支持率跌入绝对的谷底。

sentences.en: The majority of Americans do blame the Republican Party for the government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 大多数美国人确实将政府关门归咎于共和党。

sentences.en: President Obama fares much better.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统的情况要好得多。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: That was 2013.
The campaign is over.
sentences.zh: 竞选已经结束了。

sentences.en: The people of Arkansas tonight have made their choice.
sentences.zh: 阿肯色州人民今晚作出了他们的选择。

sentences.en: They had roared back.
sentences.zh: 他们卷土重来。

sentences.en: Georgia wants somebody to fight for them, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，佐治亚州需要有人为他们而战。

sentences.en: I heard that loud and clear in this state.
sentences.zh: 我在这个州清清楚楚地听到了这一点。

sentences.en: The Republicans took control of the Senate in 2014.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在2014年夺回了对参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: Tonight, we commit ourselves to building a government we can be proud of again.
sentences.zh: 今晚，我们承诺建设一个让我们再次引以为傲的政府。

sentences.en: They gained seats in the House.
sentences.zh: 他们在众议院增加了席位。

sentences.en: Tonight is looking like a very, very good night.
sentences.zh: 今晚看起来是一个非常非常美好的夜晚。

sentences.en: And the lesson that Republicans took from that is, well, you know, it wasn't pretty, but in the end, it didn't hurt.
sentences.zh: 共和党人从中吸取的教训是，好吧，虽然不好看，但到头来，它并没有造成伤害。

sentences.en: And I think Democrats are probably taking the same lesson.
sentences.zh: 我想民主党人可能也吸取了同样的教训。

sentences.en: And in fact, it didn't really hurt Republicans?
sentences.zh: 事实上，它真的没有伤害到共和党人吗？

sentences.en: It didn't.
sentences.zh: 确实没有。

sentences.en: It did not.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: I mean, it hurt them in the short run.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在短期内伤害了他们。

sentences.en: But, you know, in politics, memory is extremely short.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在政治中，记忆是极其短暂的。

sentences.en: And the events of 2013 just were not on the minds of voters when they went to the polls in November of 2014.
sentences.zh: 当选民在2014年11月走进投票站时，2013年的事件根本不在他们的脑海中。

sentences.en: Happening now, breaking news.
sentences.zh: 正在发生，突发新闻。

sentences.en: Time is running out.
sentences.zh: 时间不多了。

sentences.en: President Trump says a government shutdown could happen Friday, saying Democrats would be blamed for that.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统表示政府可能在周五关门，并称民主党人将为此受到指责。

sentences.en: And after rejecting a bipartisan immigration proposal, he now says time is running out for a deal.
sentences.zh: 在拒绝了一项两党移民提案后，他现在表示达成协议的时间已经不多了。

sentences.en: But even Republicans say they don't know what the president wants.
sentences.zh: 但就连共和党人也表示他们不知道总统想要什么。

sentences.en: So here we are in 2018, five years later, and the battle lines are around immigration rather than health care.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来到了2018年，五年后，战线围绕着移民而不是医疗保健展开。

sentences.en: But I'm struck by another difference.
sentences.zh: 但我对另一个不同点印象深刻。

sentences.en: In this case, we don't have a divided government.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们并没有一个分裂的政府。

sentences.en: The Republicans control it all.
sentences.zh: 共和党人掌控了一切。

sentences.en: We don't think of government shutdowns being a threat without a divided government.
sentences.zh: 我们不会认为在没有分裂政府的情况下政府关门会是一个威胁。

sentences.en: Well, one of the reasons we have a pending shutdown fight is because although we don't have a divided government along party lines,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们将面临关门危机的原因之一是，尽管我们在党派线上没有出现分裂的政府，

sentences.en: we have deep divisions within the Republican Party, and we have Donald Trump in the White House.
sentences.zh: 但我们在共和党内部存在严重分歧，而且白宫里有唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is a divisive figure, so divisive that he's not able to bring along Democrats even to a fairly modest proposal to keep the government open.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普是一个具有分裂性的人物，分歧如此之大，以至于他甚至无法让民主党人支持一项相当温和的保持政府运转的提案。

sentences.en: And he doesn't seem to have the ability to really rally even all the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而且他似乎也没有能力真正团结所有的共和党人。

sentences.en: Remember, some Republicans are going to vote against the spending bill as well.
sentences.zh: 记住，一些共和党人也会投票反对支出法案。

sentences.en: It's not just Democrats.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是民主党人。

sentences.en: So the president has effectively so divided the Republican Party that it's as if we have a divided government as we did back in 2013.
sentences.zh: 因此，总统实际上将共和党分裂得如此严重，就好像我们回到了2013年那样拥有一个分裂的政府。

sentences.en: We have a fractured government.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个支离破碎的政府。

sentences.en: It's more than divided because we can't even neatly draw the lines.
sentences.zh: 这比分裂更严重，因为我们甚至无法清晰地划清界限。

sentences.en: It's a mess.
sentences.zh: 这是一团糟。

sentences.en: But from what you've told us, it doesn't sound like the government shutdown in 2013 really affected the people most responsible for it, the Tea Party candidates,
sentences.zh: 但根据你所说，2013年的政府关门似乎并没有在接下来的选举中对负有最大责任的人（即茶党候选人）产生真正的影响，

sentences.en: in the following election.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的选举中。

sentences.en: So why should anyone, whether Democrats or Republicans right now, why should they worry about real repercussions for tipping us over into a new shutdown?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么任何人，无论是现在的民主党人还是共和党人，为什么要担心把我们推向新一轮关门会带来真正的后果呢？

sentences.en: I think the Republicans worry most because they're already in such bad shape.
sentences.zh: 我认为共和党人最担心，因为他们的处境已经如此糟糕。

sentences.en: President Trump is very unpopular, and we've already seen a series of special elections go to the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统非常不得人心，我们已经看到一系列特别选举被民主党人拿下。

sentences.en: Republicans need a winning streak, and they are unable to mount one.
sentences.zh: 共和党人需要一波连胜，但他们无法做到。

sentences.en: They just passed this big tax cut that was supposed to show that they could govern, and then just a few weeks later, the government shuts down.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚通过了这个本该证明他们有执政能力的大规模减税法案，结果仅仅几周后，政府就关门了。

sentences.en: That just stops their message that they are actually a party of governance.
sentences.zh: 这直接打破了他们宣称自己是执政党的宣传。

sentences.en: Democrats are in a different position.
sentences.zh: 民主党人则处在不同的位置。

sentences.en: Democrats do run a risk here,
sentences.zh: 民主党人确实在这里面临风险，

sentences.en: but they just feel like nothing will ever fall on their shoulders because the American people just tend to think that any disarray is President Trump's fault.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是觉得任何责任都不会落到自己头上，因为美国民众往往倾向于认为任何混乱都是特朗普总统的错。

sentences.en: Jonathan, thank you.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: On Thursday night, the House voted 230 to 197 to pass a temporary spending bill that would keep the government funded through February 16th.
sentences.zh: 周四晚间，众议院以230票对197票通过了一项临时开支法案，将政府资金维持至2月16日。

sentences.en: But the bill still needs Senate approval, and at least a dozen Democrats in the Senate would have to join their Republican colleagues in approving the measure.
sentences.zh: 但该法案仍需参议院批准，参议院至少需要十多名民主党人与他们的共和党同僚一起投赞成票。

sentences.en: Without protections for young undocumented immigrants, there is little chance of that happening by the deadline of midnight tonight.
sentences.zh: 如果没有对年轻无证移民的保护，今晚午夜截止日期前通过的可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: It's really almost like an amateur hour, if we're speaking about time, because this should have been done.
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论时间的话，这简直就像业余水平，因为本该早就完成了。

sentences.en: We could have come to a place where we have come to a budget agreement, as well as protecting our DREAMers, which is part of the agreement as we go forward.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以达成一项预算协议，同时保护我们的追梦人，这本来就是我们推进协议的一部分。

sentences.en: But instead, the Republicans are dilly-dallying, taking their good old time.
sentences.zh: 但相反，共和党人在磨磨蹭蹭，慢条斯理。

sentences.en: Maybe they just don't believe in governance.
sentences.zh: 也许他们根本不相信执政这回事。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the Trump administration announced that it was creating new protections for health care providers who have religious or moral objections to performing abortions,
sentences.zh: 周四，特朗普政府宣布为在进行堕胎、

sentences.en: sex change operations, or other medical services.
sentences.zh: 变性手术或其他医疗服务时有宗教或道德反对意见的医疗保健提供者建立新的保护措施。

sentences.en: As part of the plan, the White House has created a new office within the Department of Health and Human Services, the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division,
sentences.zh: 作为该计划的一部分，白宫在卫生与公众服务部内设立了一个新办公室——良心与宗教自由司，

sentences.en: and is urging people to contact the office with complaints of religious discrimination.
sentences.zh: 并敦促人们就宗教歧视投诉与该办公室联系。

sentences.en: The announcement, which came one day before today's annual March for Life in Washington, has been a priority of anti-abortion groups.
sentences.zh: 这项宣布是在华盛顿举行一年一度的生命游行前一天发布的，一直是反堕胎团体优先推动的事项。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcom, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills, Ike Sreez-Khanarajah, Claire Tennesketter, Paige Cowett, and Michael Simon-Johnson,
sentences.zh: 《每日秀》由西奥·巴尔科姆、林赛·加里森、雷切尔·奎斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯、艾克·斯里兹-卡纳拉贾、克莱尔·特内斯凯特、佩奇·考维特和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊制作，

sentences.en: with editing help from Larissa Anderson.
sentences.zh: 拉里萨·安德森提供剪辑协助。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的主编。

sentences.en: Our technical manager is Brad Fisher.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔。

sentences.en: And our sound engineer is Peter Sale.
sentences.zh: 我们的音响工程师是彼得·塞尔。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Michael Gold, Sam Dolnick, and Michaela Bouchard.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢迈克尔·戈德、萨姆·多尔尼克和米凯拉·布沙尔。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日秀》今天就到这里。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了网罗了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都会》的最新一期节目中，由我萨拉·科尼格为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在途中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都会。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
